text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Skopje press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
- Macedonian Prime Minister Branko Crvenkovski will be on an official visit to Yugoslavia on Wednesday and Thursday. He is due to meet Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic on Wednesday.
- After a three-week strike the court administration resumed work on Wednesday. The strike is suspended until September 1.

- Head of the UNPREDEP peace-keeping mission in Macedonia expressed concern over the situation in Albania and incidents at the Macedonian-Albanian border during his meeting with Debar mayor Kemal Dzafa.

- Several members of parliament of the ruling SDSM said they would not vote for the government proposal on the use of flags of national minorities, Macedonian opposition LDP party announced several amendments while ethnic Albanian parties said they would ask for Albanian flags to be used in front of all public institutions not only municipal buildings.

- An inter-party agreement has been reached to nominate Branko Naumovski, former assistant justice minister as the first ombudsman of Macedonia. Macedonian adopted the law six months ago introducing the institution of ombudsman to protect citizens in their disputes with the state. -- Mircela Casule, Skopje newsroom +389 91 201 196
